--- title: "Case Study: Humans and AI in Diagnostic Imaging" subtitle: "Introduction to Global Health Data Science" date: "2026-09-04" format: revealjs: auto-stretch: false --- ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: ## collab-CXR [collab-CXR](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40319039/) is an open-source research project that provides a collaborative framework for developing and evaluating machine learning models for chest X-ray (CXR) analysis across multiple institutions. We consider data from collab-CXR on chest x-ray detection of cardiomediastinal abnormalities, which are abnormal findings involving the heart or the mediastinum, the central compartment of the chest located between the lungs. This would include findings in the heart, great vessels, trachea, esophagus, major lymph nodes, or other soft tissues in the region. --- ## Abnormality detection Today we evaluate the quality of a machine learning (ML) or AI model trained to make a diagnosis. The ML output is in the form of the probability an abnormality is present rather than a binary diagnosis, and part of the challenge for researchers is to pick a cutoff value of the probability for determining the abnormality is indeed present. To start, let's consider a probability of 0.50 or greater as evidence that the chest x-ray is abnormal in the region of interest. --- ## AI diagnosis versus "truth"
| | **Normal** | **Abnormal** | **Total** | |---------------|:----------:|:-------------:|----------:| | **AI predicts normal** | 830 | 70 | 900 | | **AI predicts abnormal** | 251 | 145 | 396 | | **Total** | 1081 | 215 | 1296 |
--- ## Investigating the quality of AI :::: columns ::: {.column width="30%"}
| | **Normal** | **Abnormal** | **Total** | |---------------|:----------:|:-------------:|----------:| | **AI predicts normal** | 830 | 70 | 900 | | **AI predicts abnormal** | 251 | 145 | 396 | | **Total** | 1081 | 215 | 1296 |
::: ::: {.column width="5%"}   ::: ::: {.column width="65%"}
- Calculate the **sensitivity** of the AI model. - Calculate the **specificity** of the AI model. - If it is dangerous to miss a true cardiomediastinal abnormality, would you: - (a) be happy with the sensitivity and specificity, - (b) want to **increase the sensitivity**, or - (c) want to **increase the specificity**?
::: ::::

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
